title: Old-Time Squash Storage
subtitle: Tips From a USDA Farmers' Bulletin
desc: Old-time winter squash and pumpkin storage tips from a USDA Farmers' Bulletin: cure them warm, then keep them dry and cool in a single layer so they last for months. Root cellar wisdom that still works.

title: Pressure Canning Green Beans
subtitle: USDA Safe Method
desc: How to pressure can green beans safely following the USDA Complete Guide to Home Canning: 1-inch headspace, 20 minutes for pints and 25 for quarts at 10 lb (weighted gauge, sea level to 1,000 ft). Low-acid foods must never be water bath canned.

title: How to Freeze Cranberries
subtitle: Fresh Berries All Year
desc: How to freeze fresh cranberries the easy way: sort, rinse, dry and tray-freeze, then bag them for sauces, baking and smoothies all year. Simple holiday food preservation.

title: How to Store Emergency Water
subtitle: Be Ready for Winter Storms
desc: How to store emergency drinking water at home: plan one gallon per person per day for at least three days, in clean food-grade containers kept cool and dark. Easy winter storm and power outage prep.

title: Mulch Strawberries for Winter
subtitle: Protect Plants From Frost
items: Wait for a few hard frosts
desc: How to winterize strawberry plants: after a few hard frosts, cover the bed with 2–4 inches of clean straw and pull it back in spring. An easy beginner garden tip for bigger berry harvests.
